[Overview](https://usenaive.ai/docs) [Managed Agents](https://usenaive.ai/docs/concepts/agents) [API Reference](https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/overview) [SDK Reference](https://usenaive.ai/docs/sdk/typescript) [CLI Reference](https://usenaive.ai/docs/cli/overview)

Every model call goes through Naive Managed Agents’ **model router** — the ones an agent makes inside a session, and the ones you make yourself through the [model proxy](https://usenaive.ai/docs/concepts/model-router#calling-the-router-directly). The router picks the inference backend for each call based on two inputs — the **model** and the [**completion window**](https://usenaive.ai/docs/concepts/completion-window) — meters the tokens against the caller’s balance before the call runs, and returns the result. Inside a session the [harness](https://usenaive.ai/docs/how-managed-agents-is-built#the-three-layers) decides _when_ to call the model; the router — part of the [runtime](https://usenaive.ai/docs/concepts/runtime) — decides _where the call goes_ and _what it costs_.You never address a backend directly. You name a model and a window; the router does the rest. There are two ways to name them:

- **On an agent** — `model` and `window` are fields of the [agent](https://usenaive.ai/docs/concepts/agents), overridable per session. Every turn the harness runs goes through the router with them.
- **Directly** — one call, no agent and no session, through the [proxy](https://usenaive.ai/docs/concepts/model-router#calling-the-router-directly) in the Messages or Chat Completions format.

Both use the same catalogue, the same lanes and the same meter; only who pays differs. Images and video are **not** model calls: they have their own catalogue and their own pages — [Images](https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/images) and [Video](https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/video).

## [​](https://usenaive.ai/docs/concepts/model-router\#two-inference-lanes)  Two inference lanes

Managed Agents federates two inference backends behind one interface:

- **Aggregated inference network** — a broad catalogue of models available at interactive latency. This is the default lane and serves every `immediate` request.On this lane the router asks the network for the **fastest** provider that hosts the model, not the cheapest — `immediate` is the pay-for-speed window, and the default price-ordered routing was measured putting a cold first token tens of seconds out on a slow node. One consequence is worth stating plainly: because a model is hosted by several providers at different prices, **two identical `immediate` calls to the same model id can cost different amounts** depending on who served them. You are billed what the call actually cost, so the difference is real rather than an estimate — see [What a model call costs](https://usenaive.ai/docs/concepts/model-router#what-a-model-call-costs). The `priority` and `loose` windows are unaffected.
- **Completion-window pool** — specialized open-weights hosting that offers genuine reduced tariffs for the `priority` and `loose` windows at reduced latency cost. This lane serves `priority` and `loose` requests, and it only hosts a **specific set of window-supported models**.

```
 model call  (model + window)
        │
        ├─ window = immediate ─────────────▶ Aggregated inference network
        │                                     any model in the catalogue · immediate tariff
        │
        └─ window = priority | loose ──────▶ Completion-window pool
                       │                      priority / loose tariff
                       │
                       └─ model NOT window-supported ─▶ 400, refused before any spend
```

## [​](https://usenaive.ai/docs/concepts/model-router\#the-routing-rule)  The routing rule

The window determines the lane, and the lane constrains the model:

| Window | Lane | Model requirement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `immediate` | Aggregated network | Any model in the catalogue, including `vetta/auto`. |
| `priority` | Completion-window pool | Must be a **window-supported** model. |
| `loose` | Completion-window pool | Must be a **window-supported** model. |

A **non-default window** (`priority` or `loose`) with a model that the completion-window pool does not host is refused with a typed error — `window_unavailable`, **HTTP 400** — before any inference runs and before any spend. `immediate` always works, on any catalogued model. See [Errors](https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/errors).

This is a deliberate fail-closed: rather than silently downgrading a `loose` request to the interactive tariff (and quietly overcharging you), the router rejects the combination so you fix it explicitly — either pick a window-supported model, or drop to `immediate`.

## [​](https://usenaive.ai/docs/concepts/model-router\#the-catalogue-is-live)  The catalogue is live

There is **no curated list**. The catalogue is read from the inference network at request time and
cached briefly, then filtered down to the models Managed Agents can actually drive an agent with:

- text out — a model that returns images or audio is not an agent’s model;
- tool calling — the harness cannot run a loop with a model that cannot call a tool;
- a published per-token price for both prompt and completion, because a model that cannot be quoted
cannot be metered, and metering before the call is what makes spend fail closed.

That is **hundreds of models**, and it moves on its own: a model the network publishes today is
runnable today, with no release of ours. Two consequences follow for anything that reads it — the
listing is **paged**, and it is **searchable**. Nothing should assume one call returns the whole
catalogue, and nothing should hard-code a model id it has not checked.

## [​](https://usenaive.ai/docs/concepts/model-router\#discovering-models)  Discovering models

`GET /v1/models` is the catalogue; `GET /v1/models/{id}` is one entry, for the id you already hold.

CLI

API

TypeScript

```
naive models list --search glm --limit 5
naive models list --window priority          # only what that window can serve
naive models get zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8
```

```
curl -fsSL "https://api.vetta.sh/v1/models?search=glm&limit=5" \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..."

# Model ids contain a slash — percent-encode the path segment.
curl -fsSL "https://api.vetta.sh/v1/models/zai-org%2FGLM-5.2-FP8" \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..."
```

```
const page = await naive.models.list({ search: "glm", limit: 5 });
const more = await naive.models.list({ after: page.next_cursor });
const m = await naive.models.retrieve("zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8");
console.log(m.supported_windows); // ["immediate","priority","loose"]
```

| Query | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `window` | Narrow to the models that window can actually be served in — `immediate`, `priority` or `loose`. |
| `search` | Free text, matched against the model’s id and name. |
| `limit` | Page size, 1–100. Defaults to 20. |
| `after` | The previous page’s `next_cursor`. |

The listing is [cursor-paged](https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/pagination) like every other list on the API: `has_more` and
`next_cursor` are real, not constants. An id the deploy does not serve is a `not_found` (404) from
the by-id route — which makes it the cheapest way to validate a model id before you run on it.

```
{
  "object": "model",
  "id": "zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8",
  "context_window": 1048576,
  "max_output_tokens": 32768,
  "supported_windows": ["immediate", "priority", "loose"],
  "efforts": ["low", "medium", "high"]
}
```

The model object publishes **no prices** — the same line [`GET /v1/media/models`](https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/media) draws.
What you spend is bounded by the agent’s [budget](https://usenaive.ai/docs/concepts/budgets) before the call, and read back
as actuals from [`naive agent spend`](https://usenaive.ai/docs/cli/agents#spend). A published rate card would be a number to
reconcile against; the ledger is the number that is true.

`?window=` narrows to what a window can serve — the same derivation the router refuses on, so a
model listed for a window is never rejected for it.

## [​](https://usenaive.ai/docs/concepts/model-router\#max_output_tokens)  `max_output_tokens`

Every entry publishes `max_output_tokens`: the longest reply that model may produce, taken from what
the model itself advertises and clamped to a platform ceiling. It is **per model**, not one number
for the fleet — a model that can write 131 072 tokens and one that can write 8 192 are not bounded
the same way.It is also what the **pre-flight quote is bounded by**. Before a call runs, the router reserves the
worst case: every input token at the input rate, plus `max_output_tokens` at the output rate. The
call then settles at what it actually used and the remainder is released. So `max_output_tokens`
sets how much of a [budget](https://usenaive.ai/docs/concepts/budgets) one in-flight call reserves, not what it costs — a
long-output model holds more credit while it is running, and returns the difference when it is done.

## [​](https://usenaive.ai/docs/concepts/model-router\#naive-managed-agents-auto)  Naive Managed Agents Auto

`vetta/auto` is a model id like any other, and it picks the model per request: you name the task,
the router picks the model that fits it, call by call. It is useful when a workload is uneven — a
mix of trivial and hard turns — and you would rather not pin one model expensive enough for the
worst of them.

TypeScript

```
const agent = await naive.agents.create({
  name: "Triage",
  model: "vetta/auto",
  budget: { cap_micro_usd: 25_000_000, max_task_micro_usd: 3_000_000, period: "month" },
});
```

Three things are specific to it:

- **`immediate` only.** It routes across the aggregated network, so it never runs in the
completion-window pool. `priority` or `loose` with `vetta/auto` is refused with
`window_unavailable`, exactly like any other unsupported pair.
- **It is priced as a ceiling, then settled at the model that answered.** Because the model is not
known until the call is routed, there is no rate card to quote from. So the request carries a
**hard price cap** — $5 per million input tokens and $25 per million output tokens — which the
network enforces: a call it cannot serve inside the cap is refused rather than routed to something
dearer. The pre-flight hold is taken at exactly those cap rates, so it is a genuine upper bound.
The debit is then settled at the **rate of the model that actually answered**, which is normally
well below the cap. You are never billed above the ceiling you were quoted.
- **The reply names the model that answered.**`model` stays `vetta/auto`; `resolved_model` on a
[proxy](https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/proxy) reply and on a session’s `span.model_request.end` event is the model that ran.

`vetta/auto` selects a different model for different requests by design. Pin a specific id instead
when a run has to be reproducible, or when a prompt is tuned to one model’s behaviour.

## [​](https://usenaive.ai/docs/concepts/model-router\#calling-the-router-directly)  Calling the router directly

You do not need an agent to use a model. The **model proxy** is the router with nothing in front of
it: one request in, one reply out, billed to the organization. It exists for the call a session is
the wrong shape for — a classifier in your own pipeline, a one-off summary, an existing client you
would rather repoint than rewrite. Two doors, one router:

| Door | Route | Format |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Messages | [`POST /v1/proxy/anthropic/v1/messages`](https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/proxy#post-v1proxyanthropicv1messages) | The Messages request and response, `system` and `tools` included, streamed or not. |
| Chat Completions | [`POST /v1/proxy/openai/v1/chat/completions`](https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/proxy#post-v1proxyopenaiv1chatcompletions) | The Chat Completions envelope — `choices`, `finish_reason`, `usage`, `data:` chunks when streamed. |

Any id the catalogue publishes goes in `model`, `vetta/auto` included; the window travels as the
`Vetta-Window` header because neither format has a field for it, and unset means `immediate`.

TypeScript

CLI

API

```
const reply = await naive.proxy.messages(
  { model: "vetta/auto", max_tokens: 512, messages: [{ role: "user", content: "Is this ticket urgent? …" }] },
);

const chat = await naive.proxy.completions(
  { model: "zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8", messages: [{ role: "user", content: "Summarise this invoice." }] },
  "priority",
);
```

```
naive proxy message --model vetta/auto --text "Is this ticket urgent? …"
naive proxy url        # the base URL to point an existing Messages-format client at
```

```
curl -fsSL https://api.vetta.sh/v1/proxy/openai/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "authorization: Bearer sk_live_..." \
  -H "vetta-window: priority" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "model": "zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8", "messages": [{ "role": "user", "content": "Summarise this invoice." }] }'
```

What a direct call shares with an agent’s, and what it does not:

|  | Agent turn | Direct call |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Catalogue, lanes, `window_unavailable` | same | same |
| Pre-flight quote → stream → settle at actual usage | same | same |
| Who pays | the agent’s [budget](https://usenaive.ai/docs/concepts/budgets), then the org | the org balance directly — `insufficient_credits` when the quote does not fit |
| Ledger entry | carries `session_id` and `agent_id` | carries the request id (`x-request-id`) and neither |
| Tools | run by the harness inside the sandbox | returned to you as `tool_use` / `tool_calls`; you run them and send the result back |
| State between calls | the session’s durable log | none — send the whole conversation every time |
| Scope | `sessions:write` | `proxy:write` (or `sessions:write`), see [authentication](https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/authentication#scopes) |

A direct call carries **text, tools and streaming** — and refuses, as `validation_failed`, what it
cannot carry: sampling and decoding controls (`top_p`, `top_k`, `stop`, `seed`, `n`, `logprobs`,
penalties), structured output (`response_format`), `tool_choice`, extended-thinking blocks, and
image or document content parts. Nothing is dropped on the floor; a setting the router will not
honour is a call you should not pay for. The per-field detail is on the [proxy reference](https://usenaive.ai/docs/api/proxy).

## [​](https://usenaive.ai/docs/concepts/model-router\#choosing-which-model-answers)  Choosing which model answers

`vetta/auto` chooses inside the call, from the whole network. There is also an **optional add-on**
that chooses from **your** shortlist, with **your** descriptions: name two to sixteen catalogue ids,
say in a line what each is for, and an evaluation model reads the conversation and says which one
should answer it.It comes in two shapes. The first hands you the id, so you can log it or branch on it:

```
const pick = await naive.models.autoSelect({
  options: {
    "z-ai/glm-5.3-flash": "Routine coding, edits and tool use",
    "deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731": "Strict JSON output that must match a schema",
    "google/gemma-4-31B-it": "Short factual answers where speed matters",
  },
  messages,
  default: "z-ai/glm-5.3-flash",
  min_confidence: 0.5,
});
// pick.model is a concrete catalogue id — pass it as `model` on the next call.
```

The second is the same policy riding on the call itself, so the router makes the pick and the model
call in one step — per call on either proxy door, or per turn on an agent:

```
const reply = await naive.proxy.messages({
  model: "z-ai/glm-5.3-flash",              // the default; must be one of the options
  model_selection: { options: { /* as above */ }, min_confidence: 0.5 },
  max_tokens: 1024,
  messages,
});
reply.model; // the id that answered
```

Everything after the pick is the ordinary path above: the chosen id is resolved, quoted from **its**
rate card for the request’s window, admitted, routed and settled. It is an add-on, not a change to
routing — `vetta/auto`, pinned ids, windows and the catalogue behave exactly as described on this
page whether or not you use it.Full detail — the option rules, what `default` and `min_confidence` actually do, what a selection
costs and adds in latency, and how it behaves when the evaluator is unavailable — is on
[Model auto-selection](https://usenaive.ai/docs/concepts/model-selection).

## [​](https://usenaive.ai/docs/concepts/model-router\#what-a-model-call-costs)  What a model call costs

Model spend — an agent’s or a direct call’s — is metered per token across a **five-tier ledger**: each class of token is priced separately because the backends bill them separately. The request’s [completion window](https://usenaive.ai/docs/concepts/completion-window) tariff sets the rate the call is quoted and reserved at; where the backend reports what the completion actually cost, that figure is what you are billed from, so the amount tracks the provider that served the call rather than a list price for the model id.

| Token tier | Field | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Input** | `input` | Fresh prompt tokens sent to the model. |
| **Cache write** | `cache_write` | Prompt tokens written into the provider’s prompt cache. |
| **Cache read** | `cache_read` | Prompt tokens served from cache — billed at a fraction of the input rate. |
| **Output** | `output` | Tokens the model generates. |
| **Reasoning** | `reasoning` | Internal thinking tokens, when the model produces them. |

These five fields are the canonical token ledger: every inference debit records all five, and they are the components a [session’s](https://usenaive.ai/docs/concepts/sessions#cost-and-usage)`token_usage` and the billing line items are built from.

Cache-read tokens are the reason list-price rate cards mislead. A card that bills every input token at the full input rate over-states real cost by **1.017×–4.176×** depending on harness and window (see [Benchmarks](https://usenaive.ai/blogs/introducing-naive-managed-agents)). Managed Agents meters each tier at its real rate, so your bill tracks what the backend actually charged — not a rate-card fiction.

Because every call is priced against these five tiers _before_ it runs, a call that would breach your [budget](https://usenaive.ai/docs/concepts/budgets) — or, for a direct call, your balance — is refused rather than discovered on an invoice. Model spend shows up as the `model` line item in the agent’s spend breakdown:

CLI

```
naive agent spend agt_01j8rf6tq2m4vz9xkp3n7c5hwd --by component
```

```
{ "by_component": { "model": 11902000, "computer": 481000, "search": 6474, "media": 390000 } }
```

Amounts are integer micro-USD (`11902000` is $11.902). The `model` component is the sum of the five token tiers above; `computer`, `search` and `media` are the other components a debit can carry, and a component with no spend is absent rather than zero.

## [​](https://usenaive.ai/docs/concepts/model-router\#configuration-reference)  Configuration reference

[​](https://usenaive.ai/docs/concepts/model-router#param-model)

model

string

required

A model ID (e.g. `zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8`, or `vetta/auto` to pick per request). Set on the agent and overridable per [session](https://usenaive.ai/docs/concepts/sessions#override-agent-configuration-for-a-session). Any id [`GET /v1/models`](https://usenaive.ai/docs/concepts/model-router#discovering-models) publishes is legal; anything else is refused with `validation_failed` when the agent is saved. An agent has no effort setting; a model’s `efforts` list is catalogue information only.

[​](https://usenaive.ai/docs/concepts/model-router#param-window)

window

string

default:"immediate"

The [completion window](https://usenaive.ai/docs/concepts/completion-window). `immediate` routes to the aggregated network; `priority` and `loose` route to the completion-window pool and require a window-supported model.

### [​](https://usenaive.ai/docs/concepts/model-router\#read-only-model-fields)  Read-only model fields

[​](https://usenaive.ai/docs/concepts/model-router#param-context-window)

context\_window

integer

Maximum context length in tokens.

[​](https://usenaive.ai/docs/concepts/model-router#param-max-output-tokens)

max\_output\_tokens

integer

The longest reply this model may produce, and what the [pre-flight quote](https://usenaive.ai/docs/concepts/model-router#max_output_tokens) is bounded by.

[​](https://usenaive.ai/docs/concepts/model-router#param-supported-windows)

supported\_windows

string\[\]

Which windows the model can run in. `immediate` is always present; `priority`/`loose` appear only for pool-hosted models.

[​](https://usenaive.ai/docs/concepts/model-router#param-efforts)

efforts

string\[\]

Effort levels the model accepts — `low`, `medium`, `high`, or empty when it accepts none.
